analyticalNotes.kind: later editor objection, not variant or adopted authorial correction
analyticalNotes.summary: The editor disputes the argument against descending motion. A subject's coexisting potentiality, not its present actuality, can be actualized at a less perfect level. Such decline can therefore still be potentiality becoming actuality. He also questions treating withering merely as incidental motion. Preserve this disagreement alongside the author's argument.

analyticalNotes.kind: later editor cross-text objection, not variant
analyticalNotes.summary: The editor invokes Bidāya and the author's Asfar gloss: motion as motion need not have a distinct enduring substrate; substantial motion can itself be a self-subsisting fluid substantial actuality. Keep this outside authorial text.

priorUnresolvedApparatusRecord.type: Unresolved internal cross-reference · not an attested emendation
priorUnresolvedApparatusRecord.text: In Chapter IX.9, printed p. 265, the author contrasts (1) longitudinal substantial motion, where matter and the earlier form become the substrate of a later form, with (2) parallel succession, where an enduring matter receives mutually exclusive forms. The text nevertheless says «لا بطريق الخلع واللبس كما في القسم الأول، بل بطريق اللبس بعد اللبس»—'not by stripping off and putting on, as in the first kind, but by putting on after putting on'—inside its account of the FIRST (longitudinal) kind. In light of the immediately preceding distinction and the following 'first/second' conclusions, «القسم الثاني» is a plausible INTERNAL editorial conjecture for «القسم الأول». The 1417 AH printed-digital source itself reads «الأول». No independent 1404/1428 print or manuscript has been checked at this exact phrase in this review. We leave the copied Arabic and the working English unchanged, record the difficulty, and DO NOT treat the conjecture as witnessed or adopted. A future editor must report exact witness readings and any adopted before/after change.
